phase_a_scope.reader_2_reason: The paper builds and tests a model that predicts forest fire occurrence from meteorological data, i.e. it examines a wildfire hazard.

phase_a_scope.reader_2_reason: The paper addresses occupational heat stress and its health and productivity impacts on US workers and issues consensus heat safety recommendations.

phase_a_scope.reader_1_reason: The paper analyses which factors determined damage to houses exposed to two wildfires, i.e. the impacts of a fire hazard on buildings, including the role of fire weather.
phase_a_scope.reader_2_reason: The paper examines determinants of wildfire damage to 540 houses exposed to two 2013 Blue Mountains fires.

phase_a_scope.reader_2_reason: The paper builds and evaluates a wildfire burned-area prediction model for five western US locations from satellite fire and climate data.

phase_a_scope.reader_1_reason: The paper correlates urban and green-space expansion in 49 US cities with changes in heat wave frequency, duration, season and intensity, i.e. a heat hazard and its land-use drivers.

phase_a_scope.reader_1_reason: A global literature review of how bats respond to wildfire and prescribed fire, i.e. the ecological impacts of a fire hazard, including threats from more frequent and severe wildfires.
phase_a_scope.reader_2_reason: The paper reviews 52 studies of how bats respond to wildfire and prescribed fire, i.e. ecological impacts of wildfire.

phase_a_scope.reader_1_reason: The paper examines how outdoor PM2.5 air pollution limits natural-ventilation cooling hours in Indian informal settlements; heat appears through heat-index comfort thresholds and passing mentions of heat waves and heat stress, but no heat hazard or its impacts is itself examined.

phase_a_scope.reader_1_reason: The paper estimates temperature-mortality associations and district heat thresholds for South Africa to inform a heat-health warning system, i.e. the health impacts of extreme heat.
phase_a_scope.reader_2_reason: The paper examines the association between summer heat (temperature metrics) and mortality and estimates heat thresholds for South African districts.

phase_a_scope.reader_1_reason: A perspective proposing a broader framework for attributing the impacts of extreme weather events (droughts, marine heatwave, wildfires, floods) to human influence, illustrated with five case studies.
phase_a_scope.reader_2_reason: The perspective paper proposes an extreme-event-attribution framework and examines hazard events and their impacts through case studies (Kenyan drought, NE Pacific marine heatwave, 2017 Portugal fires, Venice Acqua Alta, California drought), including its own reservoir counterfactual analysis.

phase_a_scope.reader_1_reason: The paper characterizes summer heat exposure, vulnerability and heat-related mortality risk at 1,614 US prisons, i.e. exposure to and impacts of a heat hazard.
phase_a_scope.reader_2_reason: The paper evaluates summer heat exposure metrics and heat-mortality-risk days at 1,614 US prisons using gridded air temperature data.

phase_a_scope.reader_1_reason: The paper derives satellite fuel-moisture thresholds to classify wildfire hazard for an Argentine mountain range, i.e. assessment of a fire hazard for early warning.
phase_a_scope.reader_2_reason: The paper analyses pre-fire fuel moisture content against observed fires and wildfire size to set wildfire hazard thresholds in the Sierras Chicas, Argentina.

phase_a_scope.reader_1_reason: A data descriptor for a multi-method global heatwave and warm-spell record, introducing a standardized heat index and validating it on high-impact historical heatwaves.
phase_a_scope.reader_2_reason: The paper builds a global gridded heatwave/warm-spell record and uses it to characterise historical heatwave events (Chicago 1995, Europe 2003, Russia 2010).

phase_a_scope.reader_1_reason: Borderline. Mainly an IoT data-interoperability paper, but its evaluation is early wildfire detection and fire-danger assessment, tested retrospectively on a deadly 2018 wildfire in Greece.

phase_a_scope.reader_1_reason: Borderline. A statistical methods paper for bivariate exceedance isolines, motivated by and applied to fire-weather conditions (Santa Ana winds) and a deadly heat wave (Karachi, June 2015), with results on how rare those hazard conditions were.

phase_a_scope.reader_1_reason: The paper models how particulate matter from the 2007 San Diego wildland fires affected emergency department visits for respiratory illness, i.e. the health impacts of a fire hazard.
phase_a_scope.reader_2_reason: The paper models wildfire smoke particulate exposure and its association with respiratory emergency department visits during the 2007 San Diego wildland fires.
